This is Cyprian's treatise addressed to Donatus (Ad Donatum), which denounces the slaughter of war.

In Latin usage, genius is a man's guardian spirit and so his natural appetite for comfort and pleasure. To 'cheat' or 'starve one's genius' (genium defraudare) means to deny oneself the ordinary comforts of life.
A proverbial phrase for tit for tat. The English that follows, 'Go now censure…', does not render it.
